chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Joe Garland's arrangements and 'In the Mood'
summary: Garland avoided hard arrangements to suit his brother Moses, who always requested Joe's 'In the Mood', which Joe seldom played.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Joe was a pretty funny guy to work with. I mean, he run his band. But Joe was a good musician. A hell of a musician. And we used to have a lot of fun working with Joe, because a lot of the music he wouldn't play, and he had good arrangements... A lot of it he wouldn't play because of his brother's inability to play these things. His brother was not what you would call an experienced musician. I mean, he had a horn to play, he had a union card and was a member of the union. But I mean, he was not a hard-cutting musician. So Joe didn't call all them extemporaneous arrangements and things, because he knew his brother couldn't do it. It made it lighter on him and made the band sound better, too.

There was no way in the world Moses would ever play some of the arrangements that Joe made. The funny thing, Moses would always call... Moses was his little brother, and he would always call "In The Mood" -- Joe's arrangement of "In The Mood. And that's the one number that Moses could play, and that's the one number Joe wouldn't call! Then Moses called him all night long: "Joe, play 'In' The Mood,' 'In The Mood.'" See, Moses wanted Joe to play it because it's Joe's number, you know...
Well, it was a very popular number, wasn't it, at that time?
It still is! It still is. Especially after Glenn Miller made it, made a recording of it.
Well, I would think you would have the people requesting it.

No. People didn't request it. No. Not at all. See, they didn't give it any publicity. He never played it. He had it in his book, but he never played it. I guess Joe didn't like the way Moses was playing it or something. I mean, he didn't want it all messed up. Not that... You don't show off your best by having it messed up. He never played it. I don't think he played it over half-a-dozen times at the most.
